title: Costs of economic growth
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:32Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point e-growthcost covers inflation, pollution, inequality and trade deficits, but it does not teach congestion or affluenza, which the new point's brief names, and its trade-deficit card is not in the brief, so it is too different to reuse or adapt.

draft.title: Costs of economic growth
card: Economic growth is a rise in the output of an economy. It can bring benefits, but it can also bring costs.
Growth can be uneven. A boom can be followed by a bust, which can lead to job losses and falling incomes.
More production and activity can cause congestion, pollution and damage to the environment. Growth may also widen inequality if some people gain much more than others.
the stress and dissatisfaction of always wanting more goods and a higher income, even as people become richer.
draft.remember: Growth can come with costs: bust after boom, damage to the environment, wider inequality and affluenza.

opts: Stress from always wanting more as incomes rise
A rise in illness caused by factory pollution
Traffic delays caused by too many cars on roads
A gap that widens between high and low incomes
a.why: Affluenza is the stress of always wanting more, even as people become richer. The gap between high and low incomes is inequality, which is a different cost of growth.
a.clue: This cost is about how people feel, not about roads or the air.

b.q: A mining town in Western Australia grows fast. Its roads fill with trucks and commuters, and trips to work take much longer. Which cost of growth is this?
b.why: Crowded roads and longer trips are congestion, which can come with more activity and people. Affluenza is about stress from wanting more, not about traffic.
b.clue: Look at what is happening on the roads.

a.best: Stress from always wanting more as incomes rise
